exhaust-baseline-1:
The engine baseline records a nominal 54 mm bore and 54.5 mm stroke. It does not yet establish the exhaust port map, target peak-power speed or safe maximum speed. The inherited 12,000 rpm, 184° exhaust duration and 30 mm header diameter remain illustrative inputs.

The installation must run from the cylinder side directly aft toward the stern, without a forward loop. All straight models below are unwrapped centreline references. They do not establish the fit, orientation or clearance inside the hull.
exhaust-baseline-2:
Pressure disturbances and bulk gas motion are different. The animation tracks representative wave paths only; it does not calculate charge trapping, gas velocity or horsepower. Reflections are actually distributed along the cones, not concentrated at a single point. Experimental work on two-stroke exhausts examines their pressure histories and reflection timing.[1]

Fixed 575 mm effective length and assumed 450 m/s wave speed. Exhaust opening/closure: 88° / 272° ATDC, derived solely from a symmetric illustrative 184° event. Zero return lead is retained to reproduce the inherited arithmetic; it is not a recommended tuning target. At zero RPM there is no repeating engine cycle.

exhaust-baseline-4:
t = Δθ / (6N) seconds
Leff = at/2 = 1000aΔθ / (12N) mm

Using Δθ = 184°, a = 450 m/s and N = 12,000 rpm gives 2.556 ms and 575 mm. In practice the desired return can precede closure: with a lead β, this simplified illustration uses Δθ = Dexhaust − β. Engine analysis must select the useful return interval.

Lcone = |Dout − Din| / [2 tan(α/2)]
Lbelly = Leff − Lheader+duct − Ldiffuser − ½Lbaffle

Here α is the full included angle. All diameters and lengths use the same units. The midpoint is a bookkeeping approximation for a distributed reflection. In a simplified stationary temperature profile, round-trip time is 2∫dx/a(x); with steady axial flow u, the corresponding estimate becomes ∫dx/(a+u) + ∫dx/(a−u). These expressions still omit finite-amplitude, transient and distributed-reflection effects.

For an ideal gas, a = √(γRT), with absolute temperature T. Actual exhaust composition, temperature distribution and flow matter; a single temperature reading cannot qualify the entire pipe.[2]

These controls calculate a separate what-if geometry. They do not change the controlled baseline or the fixed-pipe animation above.

Diameters, header distance and cone angles stay fixed. A negative residual belly means this combination does not fit the timing estimate; do not silently force its length to zero. No torque curve or power-band width is predicted.
exhaust-baseline-5:
The jacket begins at x = 20 mm and ends at the baffle/stinger junction. Unlike the inherited drawing, it does not extend 14 mm into the stinger. Its exact span follows the recalculated chamber geometry. The first 20 mm and the stinger remain exposed in this model; their protection must be designed, not assumed.

Cooling can alter gas temperature, wave timing and downstream impedance. There is no assumption that stinger cooling or wet discharge is power-neutral. Jacket flow, pressure loss, heat rejection, drainage and expansion accommodation remain open calculations. Hull resin limits must come from the actual laminate system and cure condition.

316L is retained as a prototype candidate, not declared seawater-proof. Chloride pitting and crevice corrosion remain relevant, particularly around welds, seals and stagnant regions.[3] Material grade, weld process, passivation, flushing and inspection need qualification. A later titanium version will also need a thermal and structural review; matching geometry alone does not guarantee matching operation.
exhaust-baseline-6:
• All dimensions now derive from one calculation, rather than independent labels and mesh coordinates.
  • The dry timing reference is 651.67 mm from the stated inputs; its residual belly is recalculated.
  • The shell reaches the stated 89 mm outside diameter, with a separate water gap and wall.
  • The jacket ends at the baffle, and its length is recalculated. The stinger is consistently 216 mm.
  • Wave timing is tied to crank angle and speed, with clearly stated assumptions. No flow or power result is implied.
  • The aft-only routing decision is preserved. No fold or forward loop is introduced to force a fit.

exhaust-baseline-sources:
The three original Claude HTML artifacts are retained unchanged in the reference package. They are concept provenance, not independent validation. Engine interface context comes from WHE-KIN-001 Rev01 and the engine-first / aft-routing project decisions dated 10 October 2026.

  1. Blair & Johnston, SAE 680594 (1968); Murphy & Margolis, SAE 780708 (1978). Public abstracts consulted for scope; full papers were not reviewed.
  2. NASA Glenn: Speed of Sound. Supports the ideal-gas temperature relation, not the assumed exhaust wave speeds.
  3. Outokumpu: Corrosion resistance. Supports chloride pitting and crevice-corrosion concerns, not qualification of this pipe.

Reference pages checked 10 October 2026. All generated graphics have transparent backgrounds. No performance, hull fit, thermal margin or manufacturing approval is claimed.
